EXECUTIVE ORDER 10067
C reating  an  E m ergency  B oard to I n v e s­
tigate  a D is p u t e B e t w e e n th e M i s­
so u r i P acific  R ailroad  C o m pa n y and  
C ertain  of  I ts  E m pl o y e es
WHEREAS a dispute exists between 
the Missouri Pacific Railroad Company, 
a carrier, and certain of its employees 
represented by the Brotherhood of Loco­
motive Engineers, the Brotherhood of 
Locomotive Firemen and Enginemen, 
the Order of Railway Conductors, and 
the Brotherhood of Railroad Trainmen, 
labor organizations; and 
WHEREAS this dispute has not here­
tofore been adjusted under the provi­
sions of the Railway Labor Act, as 
amendéd; and
WHEREAS this dispute, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Board, 
threatens substantially to interrupt in­
terstate commerce within several States 
to a degree such as to deprive a large 
portion of the country of essential trans­
portation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by section 10 of 
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 
U. S. C. 160), I hereby create a board of 
three members, to be appointed by me, 
to investigate the said dispute. No mem­
ber of the said board shall be pecuniarily 
or otherwise interested in any organiza­
tion of railway employees or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to 
the President with respect to the said 
dispute within thirty days from the date 
of this order.
As provided by section 10 of the Rail­
way Labor Act, as amended, from this 
date and for thirty days after the board 
has made its report to the President, no 
change, except by agreement, shall be 
made by the Missouri Pacific Railroad 
Company or its employees in the condi­
tions out of which the said dispute arose.

Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"The order itself contains no fixed end date and no termination clause. Its report deadline (August 7, 1949, thirty days after signing on July 8, 1949) is a deadline, not an end, and the standstill that runs thirty days after the report is likewise a spent fact under the 2026-10-21 owner ruling; neither is claimed as the end. The actual report date and standstill expiry are not recorded as later events because no reviewed factual-event record for this order's report is in the packet; any report text found in the repository is unreviewed context. The dossier's chain of later events, its three selected machine searches (U.S. Code, eCFR, Federal Register catalog dispositions, each marked complete) and my reading of the held text of Executive Order 12553 show no revoking, superseding or terminating instrument before 1986-02-25.","independent_command_check":"Each command (create the board, bar interested members, require the report, freeze conditions) depends on the order and on the dispute it created; none is a separate delegation, continuing regulation or standing rule. The standstill sentence restates section 10 of the Railway Labor Act (45 U.S.C. 160); that statute is an independent source of duty and is untouched by the revocation, but the periods it measures here were set by this order's creation of the board and nothing held shows them still running.","savings_check":"Executive Order 12553 was read in full and contains no saving clause. The residual consequences of the order (the board's investigation and report, any settlement of the dispute) are not shown to depend on its continued force. Savings state none_after_bounded_search; section 10 of the Railway Labor Act continues independently as stated in the independent-command check.","scope_check":"One clause is inventoried: the whole operative text from the order heading through the standstill sentence (recitals, creation of the board, the bar on interested members, the thirty-day report requirement and the standstill). Signature, date line and any attached list identify the parties and contain no separate command. Executive Order 12553 revokes the order by number as a whole, not in part, so every command in the clause ends on the same date. The ending source cited is the revoking sentence of Executive Order 12553."}
